x.around: The city centre is walkable, with shopping malls and other administrative buildings.

hidden.d: Free maps of Mbabane and Eswatini and info on places to stay all over Eswatini.

x.intro: Mbabane is the largest city of Eswatini (formerly Swaziland). It houses Sibebe Rock, one of the biggest mountains in Africa. It sits on the banks of the Mbabane River and its tributary the Polinjane River in the Mdzimba Mountains, and was home to 95,000 people in 2010.

must.d: Nice grassy area of rolling hills and aviary activity. Walking trail. A Ramsar area.

hidden.d: Ligugu Lemaswati, a living museum consisting of a 16 hut village with traditional artifacts and livestock to portray Swazi life from the 1850s.
Historical tools and artifacts of Eswatini people. Sits on the capital grounds whereupon also lie Parliament, National Archives, and the National Church.
Sharktooth-type peak rising above high grassland ridges, waterfalls, wildlife.
A memorial honoring the first king of Swaziland, King Sobhuza II, after his death in 1982. A glass mausoleum is on the spot where the late kings body lay in state, and there is a small museum.

x.intro: Lobamba is the traditional capital of Eswatini, and home to around 11,000 citizens.

must.d: Big game viewing, hiking in the veld, Swazi cultural dances, overnight stays in beehive villages. There is a lot of wildlife from wildebeest to warthog to zebra, and crocodile. This park has a lot of natural beauty.

x.around: One can get around Manzini by bus, kombi (local, 15-passenger minibuses) or taxi. Downtown Manzini is very small and one can walk form one end to the next in 15 minutes. Getting to the residential areas such as Fairview or Ngwane Park is trickier. There are kombis that service these areas but the availability of public transport depends on how rich the neighbourhood is.

hidden.d: A market experience where you can find farm products, souvenirs, ironworks, and curios, including some things specific to Eswatini culture (beads, basketry, herbs, etc.) May not be quite as raucous as some African markets, but it…

x.intro: Manzini is the second largest city in Eswatini (Swaziland) with a population 78,000. Its sobriquet is the Hub City it is a commercial, agriculture, and navigational centre of the country. A lot of people live in settlements around the urban centre, which may not always be the best for getting lost in.

cities.d: in northern Eswatini, third city by size
capital of Shiselweni region and fourth city by size

intro: The Kingdom of Eswatini, formerly (and still commonly) known as Swaziland, is a landlocked country in Southern Africa and is informally known as "Africa in a nutshell".

x.around: You can drive around with your car in the south of the park, together with a guide. You may also use one of the park's minibuses (around E100).
x.intro: The Hlane Royal National Park in Eswatini (Swaziland) is one of the best parks in Southern Africa for tracking elephants and rhinos on foot.

x.around: Excellent walking, parts are accessible by ordinary car, but 4WD is needed for many of the tracks.

hidden.d: Viewpoint with short walks nearby, where mountain reedbuck, grey rhebok and klipspringer might be seen.
3 hours of ziplining in the Malolotja Reserve

x.intro: Malolotja Nature Reserve is in Eswatini (Swaziland). It is one of the most impressive mountain parks in Southern Africa. The spectacular scenery and the variety of fauna and flora makes it a prime highveld conservation area. It is the last unspoilt mountain wilderness left in Eswatini. The reserve extends over an area of 18 000 hectares in north-west Eswatini, making it the largest proclaimed protected area in the Kingdom.

next.d: is nearby over the border in South Africa.

x.intro: Mantenga Nature Reserve is nature park in the Ezulwini Valley of Eswatini that includes a replica 19th-century Swazi village.

Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected wildlife area in Ezulwini Valley of Swaziland, near Lobamba. It is home to a diverse array of animals, including zebras, wildebeest, impala, warthogs, and a variety of bird species.
x.safe: Staying safe at Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary involves following a few simple guidelines and being aware of your surroundings. The sanctuary is home to a variety of wild animals, including predators, so it is important to be cautious and avoid doing anything that could put yourself or the animals at risk.

x.intro: Mlawula Nature Reserve is in north-eastern Eswatini (Swaziland), covering an area of approximately 16,500 hectares. The reserve lies within the transitional zone between two biogeographic regions, the dry thorn savannas of the west, and the moister coastal thickets of the east. The reserve consists of three distinct ecological zones, the Ndzindza plateau, the Siphiso Valley and the rhyolite ridges of the western boundary.
